chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn 'Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from one who informed him, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I said to him: A man may have a shirt; may he be shrouded in it? He said, "Cut off its buttons." I said: And its sleeve? He said, "No. That is only when it was cut for him while it was new and no sleeve had been made for it. But if it is a worn garment, then do not cut anything from it except the buttons."

key_terms.أَ يُكَفَّنُ: whether the deceased may be enshrouded in it
key_terms.أَزْرَارَهُ: its buttons, which are to be removed
key_terms.الْقَمِيصُ: the shirt intended to be used for shrouding the deceased
key_terms.ثَوْبًا لَبِيسًا: a worn garment that has already been used
key_terms.جَدِيدٌ: new, referring to cloth newly prepared

ai.seo_question: If a deceased person is shrouded in his shirt, should its buttons or sleeves be cut?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding using a man's shirt as part of his shroud. It instructs that the buttons should be removed, while the sleeves should not be cut from a worn garment; cutting applies only in the specific case of a newly prepared cloth without sleeves.
